title: deploy-docs
description:
Builds agent-ops-docs/ and publishes it to GitHub Pages.

Triggers on main, not a separate docs-site branch — the auto-created
github-pages deployment environment restricts deployments to the
default branch, so a separate branch's deploy job was rejected outright
(zero steps, no logs — a hard environment-level reject, not a build
failure). Folding docs-site into main sidesteps that rather than
fighting the environment's branch-protection rule.

One-time manual setup required before this can succeed: repo Settings ->
Pages -> Build and deployment -> Source: "GitHub Actions" (no MCP/API
tool in this session's toolset can toggle that setting).

title: deploy-litellm
description:
Deploys litellm/ to Cloud Run using only GitHub Secrets — same pattern as
deploy-orchestrator.yml, added after the first litellm deploy was done
manually via gcloud from a chat session (before this pattern existed).
Trigger manually (Actions tab -> deploy-litellm -> Run workflow) or
automatically on a push to main that touches litellm/.

title: deploy-orchestrator
description:
Deploys orchestrator/ to Cloud Run using only GitHub Secrets — no
credential ever needs to be pasted into chat or stored in this repo.
Trigger manually (Actions tab -> deploy-orchestrator -> Run workflow)
or automatically on a push to main that touches orchestrator/.

title: e2e-pipeline-reusable
description:
Shared e2e test pipeline (BusyBuddy_v2#285 Phase 6). Lives here, once,
centrally - each app repo keeps only a thin caller (see
templates/e2e-pipeline-caller.yml) that passes its own install/test commands.

Shared: checkout, artifact upload, PR comment, the record_video toggle, and the
coverage requirement (tests exist and pass + every critical flow has a test,
via a per-repo manifest). Repo-specific: which test framework actually runs
(Playwright vs. Gradle/Espresso) - never hardcoded here, always an opaque
input this workflow passes through without interpreting.

needs_emulator exists because Android's instrumented tests aren't a "run a
command" problem the way Playwright is - the emulator has to be booted and
stay live for the whole test_command run, not just present beforehand. That's
the one real branch point; everything else is identical between stacks.

steps.name: Enable KVM for hardware-accelerated emulator
steps.detail: run: echo 'KERNEL=="kvm", GROUP="kvm", MODE="0666", OPTIONS+="static_node=kvm"' | sudo tee /etc/udev/rules.d/99-kvm4all.rules

steps.name: Launch emulator and wait for full boot
Run tests
steps.detail: run: RECORD_VIDEO="${{ inputs.record_video }}" TEST_COMMAND="${{ inputs.test_command }}" sh "$RUNNER_TEMP/run-emulator-tests.

steps.name: Terminate emulator
steps.detail: run: adb -s emulator-5554 emu kill || true

title: wiki-generate-reusable
description:
The shared wiki generator's actual CI logic lives here, once, centrally
(agent-ops issue #286, mirroring dev-pipeline-reusable.yml's pattern for
the dev-ticket pipeline - see that file's own header comment) - app repos
keep only a thin caller workflow (templates/wiki-caller.yml) that passes
their own site_dir/config values.

Flow: checkout the calling ("target") repo (already the default checkout
context for a workflow_call job) + this control repo (agent-ops, cross-
account, same GH App token trick as dev-pipeline-reusable.yml) -> run
scripts/wiki-generate.mjs, which reads the target repo's wiki.config.yaml
and runs only the extractors it declares -> commit any changed generated
files back to the target repo's default branch -> build the site -> ship
it to GitHub Pages via the same upload-pages-artifact/deploy-pages steps
BusyBuddy_v2's own deploy-docs.yml already uses.

steps.name: Parse control repo owner/name
steps.detail: run: IFS='/' read -r OWNER NAME <<< "${{ inputs.control_repo }}"
